AF-S1.claim: Interactive and workload admission are represented as distinct task-local circuits that converge on Security -> Gateway -> natural owner without granting authority.

AF-S2.claim: Gateway capability-scoped authorization is not yet closed.
AF-S2.blocker: Ingress currently proves a Cloudflare Access Principal, but no trusted Gateway seam supplies the Agent identity plus bounded Grant/effect authority evidence required by the existing Security Agent Admission contract.
forbiddenShortcut: Do not treat Cloudflare authentication as capability authorization.
Do not let tool arguments self-assert principal, agent, grant, scope, or approval.
Do not invent a second Gateway policy vocabulary or static allowlist as a substitute for Security-owned authorization semantics.
AF-S2.nextProof: Select one low-risk capability and bind a trusted grant/agent evidence source to Security ALLOW/STEP_UP/DENY, then enforce that exact decision at Gateway before owner routing.

AF-S3.claim: No production workload identity provider has been selected or live-bound.
AF-S3.nextProof: Use one real first-party unattended consumer; prove a non-browser workload identity and read-only capability path before adding write/execution authority.

AF-S4.claim: Existing H2 interactive OAuth/browser path remains a reference circuit, with callback transaction isolation as the invariant rather than fixed port identity.

AF-S5.claim: MCP wire-currentness is a separate interface-contract concern and is not inferred from stateless_http=True.

nonClaims: AF-S1 does not authorize any live caller.
